sentences.zh: __FORCETOC__崔融崔融，字安成，齊州全節人。

translations.literal: __FORCETOC__ Cui Rong — Cui Rong, style name Ancheng, was a native of Quanjie in Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Rong — Cui Rong, styled Ancheng, came from Quanjie in Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 擢八科高第。

translations.literal: He achieved top standing in the eight-categories examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the eight-categories examination with the highest standing.

sentences.zh: 累補宮門丞、崇文館學士。

translations.literal: He was successively appointed Palace Gate Deputy and Chongwen Hall academician.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through posts as Palace Gate Deputy and academician of the Chongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 中宗為太子時，選侍讀，典東朝章疏。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong was crown prince, he was chosen as study companion and managed the eastern palace's memorials and reports.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhongzong was still crown prince, he was selected as a study companion and oversaw the eastern palace's memorials and reports.

sentences.zh: 武后幸嵩高，見融銘《啟母碣》，歎美之。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu visited Mount Song, she saw Rong's inscription on the Qimu stele and sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu visited Mount Song, she read Rong's inscription on the Qimu stele and marveled at it.

sentences.zh: 及已封，即命銘《朝覲碑》。

translations.literal: After she had been enfeoffed, she immediately ordered him to inscribe the Chaojing stele.
translations.idiomatic: Once she had received her enfeoffment, she at once commissioned him to inscribe the Chaojing stele.

sentences.zh: 授著作佐郎，遷右史，進鳳閣舍人。

translations.literal: He was appointed Assistant in the Bureau of Historiography, promoted to Right Historian, and advanced to Drafting Attendant of the Fengge Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Assistant in the Bureau of Historiography, then promoted to Right Historian and advanced to Drafting Attendant of the Fengge Office.

sentences.zh: 時有司議關市，行人盡征之，融上疏謂：「《周官》九賦，其七曰關市。

translations.literal: At the time the relevant offices debated market tolls and taxing all travelers in full; Rong submitted a memorial saying: "The Nine Levies of the Zhou Officials, the seventh is market tolls.
translations.idiomatic: When officials proposed levying market tolls on all travelers without exception, Rong submitted a memorial: "In the Zhou Officials, of the Nine Levies, the seventh is market tolls.

sentences.zh: 以市多淫巧，而關通末遊，欲止抑之，故加稅耳。

translations.literal: Because the market has many elaborate trifles and the passes link to marginal pursuits, they wished to restrain and suppress them, and therefore added taxes.
translations.idiomatic: Markets abound in clever luxuries, and the passes draw off into minor trades; the tax was meant to curb and suppress that, not to burden everyone who passed through.

sentences.zh: 然唯斂工商，而不及往來。

translations.literal: Yet it only collected from craftsmen and merchants, and did not extend to comings and goings.
translations.idiomatic: Yet it was levied only on artisans and merchants, not on travelers passing through.

sentences.zh: 今一切通取，則事不師古。

translations.literal: Now to take universally from all would be not following antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: To collect from everyone alike now would be to abandon the ancient precedent.

sentences.zh: 且四人異業舊矣，復動而搖之。

translations.literal: Moreover the four classes have long had distinct occupations; to move again and shake them.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the four classes of people have long had their separate trades; to stir them up again would unsettle them.

sentences.zh: 市者，兼受善惡也。

translations.literal: The market receives both good and evil.
translations.idiomatic: A market takes in both the worthy and the base.

sentences.zh: 若甚，則細人無所容，細人無所容，久必為亂。

translations.literal: If it is excessive, then petty men have nowhere to lodge; if petty men have nowhere to lodge, in time there will surely be disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Press it too hard and the lowly have nowhere to stand; when they have nowhere to stand, disorder will follow in time.

sentences.zh: 天下之關必險道，市必要津，豪宗、惡少在焉，聞一旦變法，或致騷動，恐南走蠻，北走狄。

translations.literal: The passes of the realm lie on perilous routes and markets on strategic fords; powerful clans and ruffians dwell there. Hearing that the law might change overnight, they could stir unrest, and one fears they would flee south to the barbarians or north to the Di.
translations.idiomatic: The empire's passes stand on dangerous roads and its markets on vital crossings, where powerful clans and rowdies gather. Word of an abrupt change in the law could spark unrest, and they might flee south to the barbarians or north to the Di.

sentences.zh: 今江津、河滸列鋪率稅，檢覆稽留，加主司僦略邀丐，則商人廢業。

translations.literal: Now at river crossings and river banks posts are set up to levy taxes at a fixed rate, inspections delay travelers, and on top of this the supervising officials extort and beg—then merchants abandon their trade.
translations.idiomatic: Today at river crossings and along the banks, tax posts levy at a fixed rate, inspections hold travelers up, and supervising officials extort and beg on the side—until merchants give up their trade altogether.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉、齊、隋所不行，況陛下乎？

translations.literal: What Wei, Jin, Qi, and Sui did not carry out—how much less should Your Majesty?
translations.idiomatic: Wei, Jin, Qi, and Sui never went this far—how much less should Your Majesty?

sentences.zh: 有如師興費廣，雖倍算商旅、加斂齊人可也。

translations.literal: If armies are raised and expenses are great, even doubling the levies on traveling merchants and adding exactions on the people of Qi would be acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: If armies must be raised and costs mount, then even doubling tolls on traveling merchants and levying extra on the people of Qi would be tolerable.

sentences.zh: 」後納之。

translations.literal: " Later this was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: " The court later adopted his advice.

sentences.zh: 張易之兄弟頗延文學士，融與李嶠、蘇味道、麟台少監王紹宗降節佞附。

translations.literal: The Zhang Yizhi brothers greatly gathered literary scholars; Rong, together with Li Jiao, Su Weidao, and Vice Director of the Lin Terrace Wang Shaozong, lowered themselves in demeanor to fawn and attach.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhang Yizhi brothers cultivated literary men about them; Rong, Li Jiao, Su Weidao, and Vice Director of the Lin Terrace Wang Shaozong all humbled themselves to flatter and court them.

sentences.zh: 易之誅，貶袁州刺史。

translations.literal: When Yizhi was executed, Rong was demoted to prefect of Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Yizhi was put to death, Rong was demoted to prefect of Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 召授國子司業。

translations.literal: He was recalled and appointed Vice Director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and appointed Vice Director of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 與脩《武后實錄》勞，封清河縣子。

translations.literal: For his labor in compiling the Veritable Records of Empress Wu, he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Qinghe county.
translations.idiomatic: For helping compile the Veritable Records of Empress Wu, he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 融為文華婉，當時未有輩者。

translations.literal: Rong's writing was florid and graceful; at the time there was no one of his generation.
translations.idiomatic: Rong wrote in a florid, graceful style unmatched in his day.

sentences.zh: 朝廷大筆，多手敕委之，其《洛出寶圖頌》尤工。

translations.literal: For great compositions of the court, many were entrusted to him by imperial autograph edict; his "Eulogy on the Treasure Chart Emerging from the Luo" was especially accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: The court's weightiest compositions were often assigned to him by autograph edict; his "Eulogy on the Treasure Chart Emerging from the Luo" was especially fine.

sentences.zh: 譔《武后哀冊》最高麗，絕筆而死，時謂思苦神竭雲。

translations.literal: When he composed the Lament for Empress Wu it was most lofty and beautiful; he died as soon as he laid down the brush, and at the time they said his thought had been bitter and his spirit exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: He composed the Lament for Empress Wu in the loftiest style and died the moment he set down his brush; people said his mind had been wrung dry and his spirit spent.

sentences.zh: 年五十四。

translations.literal: He was fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 贈衛州刺史，諡曰文。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Prefect of Weizhou, with posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Prefect of Weizhou and given the posthumous title Wen.

sentences.zh: 膳部員外郎杜審言為融所獎引，為服緦麻。

translations.literal: Du Shenyan, Vice Director of the Board of Provisions, had been promoted by Rong; he wore the finest hemp mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Du Shenyan of the Board of Provisions, whom Rong had championed, wore the finest grade of mourning for him.

sentences.zh: 六子，其聞者禹錫、翹。

translations.literal: He had six sons; those known were Yuxi and Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: He had six sons; those who became known were Yuxi and Qiao.

sentences.zh: 禹錫，開元中，中書舍人，贈定州刺史，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: Yuxi, in the Kaiyuan era, was Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat; posthumously made Prefect of Dingzhou, with posthumous title Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Yuxi served as Secretariat Drafting Attendant under Kaiyuan and was posthumously made Prefect of Dingzhou with the posthumous title Zhen.

sentences.zh: 翹，禮部尚書，贈荊州大都督，諡曰成。

translations.literal: Qiao was Minister of Rites; posthumously made Grand Protector-General of Jingzhou, with posthumous title Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao rose to Minister of Rites and was posthumously made Grand Protector-General of Jingzhou with the posthumous title Cheng.

sentences.zh: 孫巨，右補闕，亦有文。

translations.literal: His grandson Ju was Right Remonstrance Censor and also had literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Ju served as Right Remonstrance Censor and was likewise accomplished in letters.

sentences.zh: 曾孫 從曾孫從。

translations.literal: Great-grandson Cong.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandson was Cong.

sentences.zh: 從字子乂，少孤貧，與兄能偕隱太原山中。

translations.literal: Cong, style name Ziyi, was orphaned young and poor; with his elder brother Neng he retired together to the mountains of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Cong, styled Ziyi, lost his father early and grew up poor; he and his elder brother Neng withdrew together to the mountains of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 會歲饑，拾橡實以飯，講學不廢。

translations.literal: When famine came, they gathered acorns for food but did not abandon their lectures and study.
translations.idiomatic: In a year of famine they lived on gathered acorns yet never stopped their lectures and study.

sentences.zh: 擢進士第。

translations.literal: He achieved the jinshi degree.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 從山南嚴震府為推官，以母喪免。

translations.literal: Cong served in the staff of Yan Zhen of Shannan as investigating officer, and left office on his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: Cong served on Yan Zhen's staff in Shannan as investigating officer until he left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 兄弟廬墓，手藝松柏。

translations.literal: The brothers built a mourning hut by the tomb and with their own hands planted pines and cypresses.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers kept vigil by the tomb and planted pines and cypresses with their own hands.

sentences.zh: 喪闋，不應辟命。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he did not respond to summons.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, he declined every summons to office.

sentences.zh: 久之，韋皋引為西山運務使。

translations.literal: After a long time, Wei Gao brought him in as Commissioner for Western Mountain transport.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually Wei Gao brought him in as Commissioner for Western Mountain transport.

sentences.zh: 奏遷判官，攝守邛州。

translations.literal: He memorialized for promotion to staff judge and acted as acting prefect of Qiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to staff judge and served as acting prefect of Qiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 前刺史有以盜繫獄，辭已具。

translations.literal: The former prefect had been imprisoned on a charge of theft; the confession was already complete.
translations.idiomatic: The former prefect sat in prison on a theft charge with a confession already on record.

sentences.zh: 從疑其冤，縱不治，俄得真盜。

translations.literal: Cong suspected injustice, released him without prosecuting, and soon the real thief was caught.
translations.idiomatic: Cong suspected a miscarriage of justice, released the man without proceeding, and soon caught the real thief.

sentences.zh: 皋卒，劉辟反，欲並東川。

translations.literal: When Gao died, Liu Pi rebelled and wished to annex Dongchuan.
translations.idiomatic: After Gao died, Liu Pi rebelled and sought to annex Dongchuan.

sentences.zh: 從以書諭止辟，辟怒，從乃募兵嬰城守。

translations.literal: Cong sent a letter admonishing Pi to stop; Pi grew angry, and Cong then raised troops to hold the city.
translations.idiomatic: Cong wrote urging Pi to desist; when Pi flew into a rage, Cong raised troops and held the city.

sentences.zh: 辟方悉兵拒高崇文，戰而敗，從完州自如。

translations.literal: Pi had just marshaled all his troops to resist Gao Chongwen, fought and was defeated; Cong's prefecture remained intact as before.
translations.idiomatic: Pi had thrown all his forces against Gao Chongwen, lost the battle, and Cong's prefecture emerged unscathed.

sentences.zh: 盧坦表宣州副使。

translations.literal: Lu Tan recommended him as Vice Commissioner of Xuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Tan recommended him for the post of Vice Commissioner of Xuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 入為殿中侍御史，遷吏部員外郎。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Attending Censor in the Palace, and was promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as Palace Attending Censor and was promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 異時，史給選者成牒，以先後丐賕，從一限出之，後遂為法。

translations.literal: In former times, when the clerks issued selection documents, they begged bribes according to priority; Cong issued them all at one deadline, and afterward this became the rule.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly clerks handing out appointment documents solicited bribes according to who came first; Cong released them all on a single deadline, and the practice thereafter became law.

sentences.zh: 裴度為御史中丞，奏以右司郎中知雜事。

translations.literal: When Pei Du was Censor-in-Chief, he memorialized that Cong, as Right Department Director, should handle miscellaneous censorial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Du served as Censor-in-Chief, he had Cong, as Right Department Director, take charge of miscellaneous censorial business.

sentences.zh: 度已相，代為中丞。

translations.literal: When Du had become chancellor, Cong replaced him as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Once Du had become chancellor, Cong succeeded him as Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 所彈治，不屈權幸。

translations.literal: In his impeachments and prosecutions he did not yield to the powerful and favored.
translations.idiomatic: In impeachment and prosecution he never bowed to the powerful or the favored.

sentences.zh: 事系台閣而付仗內者，必請還有司。

translations.literal: Matters belonging to the Censorate but handed to the inner palace guard office—he always requested they be returned to the proper offices.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a case belonged to the Censorate but was handed to the inner palace guards, he insisted it be returned to the proper offices.

sentences.zh: 薦引御史，務取質重廉退者。

translations.literal: In recommending censors he strove to select those of solid character who were retiring and incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: In recommending censors he sought men of solid character who were retiring and incorrupt.

sentences.zh: 李翛以寵得京兆尹，為莊憲太后山陵橋道使，務以減末徭費為功，至不治道輴車留渭橋，久不得進。

translations.literal: Li Xiao, through favor, became Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao and Commissioner for bridges and roads at the mausoleum of Empress Zhuangxian; he made it his merit to cut minor corvée expenses, to the point of not maintaining the road so that the imperial hearse was held up at Wei Bridge and long could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiao won favor and became Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao and Commissioner for the bridges and roads at Empress Zhuangxian's mausoleum; he prided himself on trimming minor corvée costs until he neglected the road and the imperial hearse was stranded at Wei Bridge for a long time.

sentences.zh: 從三劾之，無少貸。

translations.literal: Cong impeached him three times without the least leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Cong impeached him three times and showed no leniency whatsoever.

sentences.zh: 俄授陝虢觀察使。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Observation Commissioner of Shan-Guo.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Observation Commissioner of Shan-Guo.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書右丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 王承宗請割德、棣而遣子入侍也，憲宗選堪使者，以命從。

translations.literal: Wang Chengzong requested to cede De and Di and send his son to attend court; Xianzong chose a capable envoy and assigned Cong.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Chengzong offered to surrender De and Di and send his son to court, Xianzong chose a capable envoy and sent Cong.

sentences.zh: 議者謂承宗狠譎，非單使可屈。

translations.literal: Discussants said Chengzong was fierce and crafty and could not be bent by a lone envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Critics said Chengzong was fierce and treacherous and could not be swayed by a lone envoy.

sentences.zh: 次魏，田弘正請以五百騎從，辭之，惟童騎十數，疾趨鎮。

translations.literal: Stopping at Wei, Tian Hongzheng requested to accompany him with five hundred horsemen; he declined, taking only a dozen or so mounted youths and hurrying to the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At Wei, Tian Hongzheng offered five hundred horsemen as escort; Cong declined and rode on with only a dozen youths, pressing swiftly to the commandery seat.

sentences.zh: 集軍士球場宣詔，為陳逆順大節禍福之效，音辭暢厲，士感動，承宗自失，貌愈恭，至泣下，即按二州戶口、符印上之。

translations.literal: He assembled the troops on the ball ground to proclaim the edict, expounding the great principle of obedience and rebellion and the effects of fortune and misfortune; his voice and words were clear and forceful, the soldiers were moved, Chengzong lost himself, his bearing grew ever more respectful, even to weeping, and he immediately submitted the household registers and seals of the two prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered the troops on the drill ground to proclaim the edict and set forth the great moral of loyalty and rebellion and the wages of fortune and ruin; his voice rang clear and stern, the soldiers were stirred, Chengzong lost his composure, grew ever more deferential, even to tears, and at once surrendered the household registers and seals of the two prefectures.

sentences.zh: 還為山南西道節度使。

translations.literal: On his return he became Military Governor of Shannan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made Military Governor of Shannan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 帝欲遂相，監軍使揣知，為用事者求金，從不肯答，用是不得相。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to make him chancellor; the army supervisory commissioner guessed this and sought gold on behalf of the power-holders; Cong refused to answer, and for this reason did not become chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor meant to make him chancellor; the army supervisory commissioner guessed as much and solicited gold on behalf of the power-holders; Cong would not comply, and for that reason never reached the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 長慶初，繇尚書左丞領鄜坊節度。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Changqing, proceeding from Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs he took command of the Bian-Fang circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Changqing he moved from Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs to command the Bian-Fang circuit.

sentences.zh: 屬部多神策屯軍，數亂法驕橫，吏不能制，從一繩以法，下皆重足畏之。

translations.literal: His subordinate territory had many encamped Shence Army troops who repeatedly violated the law in arrogant insolence and whom officials could not control; Cong applied the law uniformly, and below all walked with overlapping feet in fear of him.
translations.idiomatic: His jurisdiction held many encamped Shence troops who repeatedly broke the law in arrogant defiance and whom local officials could not restrain; Cong applied the law without exception, and all below walked in fear of him.

sentences.zh: 党項互市羊馬，類先遺帥守，從獨不取，而厚慰待之，羌不敢盜境。

translations.literal: When the Tangut traded sheep and horses at the border markets, it was customary first to give gifts to the prefect and defenders; Cong alone did not take them but treated them generously with comfort, and the Qiang did not dare raid the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: When Tanguts traded sheep and horses at the border markets, prefects and garrison commanders usually took gifts first; Cong alone refused gifts and treated them generously instead, and the Qiang did not dare raid his frontier.

sentences.zh: 寶曆初，為東都留守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoli he was made Eastern Capital Regent.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Baoli he was appointed Eastern Capital Regent.

sentences.zh: 故事，留司官入宮城門列晨衙見留守。

translations.literal: By precedent, officials of the resident administration entered the palace city gate and lined up for the morning audience to see the regent.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, resident officials entered the palace gate and lined up for the morning audience with the regent.

sentences.zh: 吏誕傲，久廢，至是復行。

translations.literal: The clerks had grown insolent and the practice had long been abandoned; now it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks had grown arrogant and the practice had long lapsed; Cong restored it.

sentences.zh: 召拜戶部尚書。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 宰相李宗閔以從裴度、李德裕所善，內不喜。

translations.literal: The chancellor Li Zongmin, because Cong was favored by Pei Du and Li Deyu, inwardly disliked him.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Li Zongmin disliked Cong inwardly because Pei Du and Li Deyu favored him.

sentences.zh: 從求致仕，除太子賓客，分司東都，告滿百日去。

translations.literal: Cong requested retirement; he was made Guest of the Heir Apparent with a commission at the Eastern Capital, and after the hundred-day notice period he departed.
translations.idiomatic: Cong asked to retire and was made Guest of the Heir Apparent with a commission at the Eastern Capital; after the hundred-day notice he left office.

sentences.zh: 於是眾嘩語不平，宗閔懼，復授檢校尚書左僕射、淮南節度副大使，知節度事。

translations.literal: Thereupon the crowd clamored in discontent; Zongmin grew afraid and again appointed him Acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Vice Military Governor of Huainan, with charge of circuit affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The public clamored in protest; Zongmin grew alarmed and reappointed him Acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Vice Military Governor of Huainan with charge of circuit affairs.

sentences.zh: 揚州凡交易貲產、奴婢有貫率錢，畜羊有口算，又貿曲牟其贏，以佐用度，從皆蠲除之。

translations.literal: At Yangzhou, for all transactions in goods and property and sales of slaves and servants there was a standard-rate levy; for keeping sheep there was a per-head tax; moreover they traded in yeast to mulct the profits to supplement expenses—Cong abolished all of these.
translations.idiomatic: At Yangzhou every transaction in goods or property and every sale of slaves carried a standard levy, sheep were taxed by the head, and officials traded in yeast to skim profits for expenses; Cong abolished all of it.

sentences.zh: 官吏俸帛常加倍以給，獨節度使則否，從皆與之同。

translations.literal: Officials' salary silks were commonly given at double the standard, but the military governor alone was not; Cong gave him the same as the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Officials' salary silks were commonly paid at double the standard, but military governors alone were not; Cong paid himself the same as everyone else.

sentences.zh: 大和六年卒，年七十二。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Dahe he died, aged seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year of Dahe, at seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 下有刲股肉以祭者。

translations.literal: Among his subordinates were those who cut flesh from their thighs to offer in sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Some of his subordinates cut flesh from their thighs for funeral sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 贈司空，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Minister of Works, with posthumous title Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Minister of Works with the posthumous title Zhen.

sentences.zh: 從為人嚴偉，立朝棱棱有風望，不喜交權利，忠厚而讓。

translations.literal: Cong as a man was stern and imposing; in court he stood angular with commanding presence, disliked associating with power and profit, and was loyal, generous, and yielding.
translations.idiomatic: Cong was stern and imposing; in court he carried himself with sharp dignity, shunned dealings in power and profit, and was loyal, generous, and self-effacing.

sentences.zh: 階品當立門戟，終不請。

translations.literal: His rank entitled him to gate halberds, but he never requested them.
translations.idiomatic: His rank entitled him to ceremonial gate halberds, but he never asked for them.

sentences.zh: 位方鎮，內無聲妓娛玩。

translations.literal: Though he held a frontier command, within he had no singing girls or diversions.
translations.idiomatic: Though he held a frontier command, he kept no singing girls or diversions within his household.

sentences.zh: 士大夫賢之。

translations.literal: Scholar-officials esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Scholar-officials held him in esteem.

sentences.zh: 曾孫 能能，字子才。

translations.literal: Great-grandson Neng — Neng, style name Zicai.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandson was Neng — Neng, styled Zicai.

sentences.zh: 硃泚之亂，渾瑊以朔方軍戰武功，引佐幕府。

translations.literal: In the rebellion of Zhu Ci, Hun Jian fought at Wugong with the Shuofang army and brought Neng in to assist his staff headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhu Ci's rebellion, Hun Jian fought at Wugong with the Shuofang army and brought Neng onto his staff.

sentences.zh: 進累侍御史。

translations.literal: He advanced through successive posts as Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts as Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 河東鄭儋表為判官。

translations.literal: Zheng Dan of Hedong recommended him as staff judge.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Dan of Hedong recommended him as staff judge.

sentences.zh: 累遷黔中觀察使，以讒坐貶。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to Observation Commissioner of Qianzhong and, on a slander charge, was demoted.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Observation Commissioner of Qianzhong but was demoted on a slander charge.

sentences.zh: 從為中丞，奏以自代。

translations.literal: When Cong was Censor-in-Chief, he memorialized recommending Neng to succeed himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Cong became Censor-in-Chief, he memorialized recommending Neng as his successor.

sentences.zh: 繇將作監授嶺南節度使，與從皆秉節居鎮，世傳為榮。

translations.literal: Proceeding from Director of the Directorate for Palace Buildings, he was made Military Governor of Lingnan; he and Cong both held staffs and governed commands—a glory handed down in the family.
translations.idiomatic: From Director of the Directorate for Palace Buildings he was made Military Governor of Lingnan; he and Cong both held frontier commands, a distinction the family passed down with pride.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十八，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He died, aged sixty-eight, and was posthumously made Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-eight and was posthumously appointed Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 從子慎由、安潛。

translations.literal: Cong's nephews were Shenyou and An Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Cong's nephews were Shenyou and An Qian.

sentences.zh: 能子彥曾。

translations.literal: Neng's son was Yanzeng.
translations.idiomatic: Neng's son was Yanzeng.

sentences.zh: 能從子 慎由慎由，字敬止。

translations.literal: Neng's nephew Shenyou — Shenyou, style name Jingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Neng's nephew Shenyou — Shenyou, styled Jingzhi.

sentences.zh: 聰警強記，資端厚，有父風采。

translations.literal: He was clever and alert with a strong memory, his nature upright and generous, and had his father's bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and alert with a formidable memory, upright and generous in character, he bore his father's presence.

sentences.zh: 繇進士第擢賢良方正異等。

translations.literal: Proceeding from the jinshi degree, he was advanced to outstanding grade in the Worthy and Upright examination.
translations.idiomatic: After taking the jinshi degree, he was advanced to outstanding grade in the Worthy and Upright examination.

sentences.zh: 鄭滑高銖辟府判官。

translations.literal: Gao Chu of Zheng-Hua recruited him as staff judge.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Chu of Zheng-Hua recruited him as staff judge.

sentences.zh: 入為右拾遺，進翰林學士。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Right Reminder and was advanced to Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as Right Reminder and was advanced to Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 授湖南觀察使。

translations.literal: He was appointed Observation Commissioner of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Observation Commissioner of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 召還，由刑部侍郎領浙西。

translations.literal: He was recalled; proceeding from Vice Minister of Justice he took charge of Zhexi.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and, as Vice Minister of Justice, took charge of Zhexi.

sentences.zh: 入遷戶部侍郎，判戶部。

translations.literal: He entered the capital and was promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue with charge of the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as Vice Minister of Revenue with charge of the ministry.

sentences.zh: 始，慎由苦目疾，不得視，醫為治刮，適愈而召。

translations.literal: At first Shenyou suffered from eye disease and could not see; physicians treated him by scraping, and just as he recovered he was summoned.
translations.idiomatic: Shenyou had long suffered from eye disease and could not see; physicians scraped his eyes to treat him, and he had just recovered when the summons came.

sentences.zh: 俄進工部尚書、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to Minister of Works and Associate Chief Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Minister of Works and Associate Chief Councilor.

sentences.zh: 與蕭鄴有隙，鄴輔政，引劉瑑，而出慎由為東川節度使。

translations.literal: He had a rift with Xiao Ye; when Ye assisted in government he brought in Liu Zhuan and sent Shenyou out as Military Governor of Dongchuan.
translations.idiomatic: He feuded with Xiao Ye; when Ye took power he brought in Liu Zhuan and posted Shenyou out as Military Governor of Dongchuan.

sentences.zh: 初，宣宗餌長年藥，病渴且中躁，而國嗣未立。

translations.literal: At first Xuanzong took longevity medicines, suffered thirst and inner agitation, and the heir to the state had not been established.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong had been taking longevity elixirs, suffered raging thirst and inner agitation, and still had not named an heir.

sentences.zh: 帝對宰相欲肆赦，患無其端。

translations.literal: The emperor told the chancellors he wished to proclaim a general amnesty but worried there was no occasion for it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his chancellors he wished to proclaim a general amnesty but could find no suitable occasion.

sentences.zh: 慎由曰：「太子，天下本。

translations.literal: Shenyou said: "The crown prince is the root of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Shenyou said, "The crown prince is the foundation of the realm.

sentences.zh: 若立之，赦為有名。

translations.literal: If he is established, the amnesty will have a proper name.
translations.idiomatic: If you invest him, the amnesty will have a proper justification.

sentences.zh: 」帝惡之，不答。

translations.literal: " The emperor disliked this and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor took offense and made no reply.

sentences.zh: 鄴等乘是譖去之，時大中十二年也。

translations.literal: Ye and others seized on this to slander him out of office; it was the twelfth year of Dazhong.
translations.idiomatic: Ye and his allies used the remark to slander him out of office; this was the twelfth year of Dazhong.

sentences.zh: 咸通初，徙華州刺史，改河中節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiantong he was transferred to Prefect of Huazhou and then made Military Governor of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xiantong he was transferred to Prefect of Huazhou, then made Military Governor of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 以吏部尚書請老，授太子太保，分司東都。

translations.literal: As Minister of Personnel he requested retirement and was made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent with a commission at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: As Minister of Personnel he asked to retire and was made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent with a commission at the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈司空，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Minister of Works, with posthumous title Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously appointed Minister of Works with the posthumous title Zhen.

sentences.zh: 子胤，別傳。

translations.literal: His son Yin has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yin is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 能從子 安潛安潛，字進之。

translations.literal: Neng's nephew An Qian — An Qian, style name Jinzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Neng's nephew An Qian — An Qian, styled Jinzhi.

sentences.zh: 進士擢第。

translations.literal: He achieved the jinshi degree.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 咸通中，曆江西觀察、忠武節度使。

translations.literal: During Xiantong he successively served as Observation Commissioner of Jiangxi and Military Governor of Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xiantong he served as Observation Commissioner of Jiangxi and then Military Governor of Zhongwu.

sentences.zh: 乾符初，王仙芝寇河南，安潛募人增陴繕械，不以力費仰朝廷。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianfu, Wang Xianzhi raided Henan; An Qian recruited men, heightened walls, and repaired weapons without relying on the court for labor expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianfu, when Wang Xianzhi raided Henan, An Qian recruited troops, raised the walls, and repaired arms without asking the court to bear the cost.

sentences.zh: 首請會兵討捕，號令精明，賊畏之，不犯陳許境。

translations.literal: He was the first to request combined forces to pursue and capture them; his orders were sharp and clear, the bandits feared him, and they did not invade the Chen-Xu region.
translations.idiomatic: He was first to call for combined forces to hunt the rebels; his orders were crisp and exact, the bandits feared him, and they did not cross into Chen-Xu.

sentences.zh: 使大將張自勉將兵七千援宋州。

translations.literal: He sent his great general Zhang Zimian with seven thousand troops to relieve Songzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his chief general Zhang Zimian with seven thousand men to relieve Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 時宋威屯曹州，而官軍數卻，賊圍宋益急。

translations.literal: At the time Song Wei was encamped at Caozhou, but government troops had repeatedly retreated and the bandits pressed the siege of Song ever tighter.
translations.idiomatic: Song Wei was then encamped at Caozhou, but government troops had fallen back repeatedly and the rebels tightened their siege of Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 自勉收南月城，斬賊二千級，仙芝夜解去。

translations.literal: Zimian recovered Nanyue city and beheaded two thousand bandits; Xianzhi lifted the siege by night and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Zimian retook Nanyue city and killed two thousand rebels; Xianzhi raised the siege overnight and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 宰相鄭畋建言：「請以陳許兵三千隸宋威。

translations.literal: The chancellor Zheng Tian proposed: "Please assign three thousand Chen-Xu troops to Song Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Zheng Tian proposed, "Assign three thousand Chen-Xu troops to Song Wei.

sentences.zh: 」而威忌自勉，乞盡得安潛軍，使自勉隸麾下。

translations.literal: " But Wei resented Zimian and requested to receive all of An Qian's army and have Zimian placed under his command.
translations.idiomatic: " But Wei resented Zimian and asked to take all of An Qian's troops and place Zimian under his own command.

sentences.zh: 畋謂威有疑忿，必殺自勉，奏言：「今以兵悉畀威，是自勉以功受辱。

translations.literal: Tian said Wei harbored suspicion and resentment and would surely kill Zimian; he memorialized: "Now to give all the troops to Wei is to let Zimian be shamed despite his merit.
translations.idiomatic: Tian said Wei nursed suspicion and would surely kill Zimian; he memorialized, "To hand him every soldier now is to let Zimian be disgraced for his victory.

sentences.zh: 安潛抗賊有功，乃取銳兵付威，後有緩急，何以戰？

translations.literal: An Qian resisted the bandits with merit, yet his elite troops are given to Wei—when urgency comes later, with what will he fight?
translations.idiomatic: An Qian has fought the rebels with success, yet you would strip him of his best troops for Wei—when the next crisis comes, how will he fight?

sentences.zh: 是勞不蒙賞，無以示天下。

translations.literal: This is labor unrewarded, with no way to show the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Toil would go unrewarded, and the court would have no example to show the realm.

sentences.zh: 」詔止以四千付威，餘還自勉。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered only four thousand given to Wei; the rest returned to Zimian.
translations.idiomatic: " The edict gave Wei only four thousand men and returned the rest to Zimian.

sentences.zh: 俄代高駢領西川節度。

translations.literal: Soon he replaced Gao Pian in command of the Xichuan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He soon replaced Gao Pian as Military Governor of Xichuan.

sentences.zh: 吏倚駢為奸利者，安潛皆誅之，數更除繆政，於是盜賊衰，蜀民以安。

translations.literal: Officials who had relied on Pian for corrupt profit—An Qian executed them all, repeatedly abolished mistaken policies, and thereafter bandits declined and the people of Shu were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: He executed every official who had profited through Pian's patronage, repealed one bad policy after another, and banditry waned until the people of Shu lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 宰相盧攜素厚駢，乃誣以罪，罷為太子賓客，分司東都。

translations.literal: The chancellor Lu Xie had long been close to Pian and therefore slandered An Qian with crimes; he was dismissed as Guest of the Heir Apparent with a commission at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Lu Xie, who had long favored Pian, framed An Qian on false charges and dismissed him as Guest of the Heir Apparent with a commission at the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 僖宗避賊劍南，召為太子少師。

translations.literal: When Xizong fled the bandits to Jiannan, An Qian was summoned as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Xizong fled the rebels to Jiannan, An Qian was summoned as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 王鐸任都統，表以自副。

translations.literal: When Wang Duo served as supreme commander, he memorialized recommending An Qian as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Duo served as supreme commander, he recommended An Qian as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 鐸解兵，安潛復為少師、東都留守。

translations.literal: When Duo relinquished command, An Qian again became Junior Tutor and Eastern Capital Regent.
translations.idiomatic: When Duo laid down command, An Qian again became Junior Tutor and Eastern Capital Regent.

sentences.zh: 青州王敬武卒，詔拜平盧節度使，檢校太師兼侍中。

translations.literal: When Wang Jingwu of Qingzhou died, an edict appointed An Qian Military Governor of Pinglu, Acting Grand Preceptor and Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jingwu of Qingzhou died, the court appointed An Qian Military Governor of Pinglu with the acting titles Grand Preceptor and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 會敬武子師範專地，不得入而還。

translations.literal: But Jingwu's son Shifan held the territory exclusively; unable to enter, he returned.
translations.idiomatic: But Jingwu's son Shifan held the territory himself; unable to take up the post, An Qian turned back.

sentences.zh: 後遷太子太傅。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太子太師，諡貞孝。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, with posthumous title Zhenxiao.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously appointed Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous title Zhenxiao.

sentences.zh: 安潛于吏事尤長，雖位將相，閱具獄，未嘗不身聽之。

translations.literal: An Qian was especially skilled in administrative matters; though he reached the rank of general or minister, when reviewing completed cases he never failed to hear them in person.
translations.idiomatic: An Qian excelled at administrative work; even at ministerial rank he personally heard every completed case brought before him.

sentences.zh: 能子 彥曾彥曾，咸通初，繇太僕卿為徐州觀察使。

translations.literal: Neng's son Yanzeng — Yanzeng, at the beginning of Xiantong proceeding from Director of the Imperial Stud, became Observation Commissioner of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Neng's son Yanzeng — early in Xiantong Yanzeng moved from Director of the Imperial Stud to Observation Commissioner of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 曉律令，然卞急，為政剛猛。

translations.literal: He understood statutes and ordinances, but was impetuous; in government he was harsh and severe.
translations.idiomatic: He knew the law codes well but was impetuous and governed with harsh severity.

sentences.zh: 徐軍素驕，而彥曾長於撫民，短治軍，士多怨之。

translations.literal: The Xuzhou army had long been arrogant, while Yanzeng was skilled at comforting the people but weak at governing troops; the soldiers largely resented him.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuzhou army had long been unruly; Yanzeng was good with civilians but poor with troops, and the soldiers resented him.

sentences.zh: 初，蠻寇五管，陷交趾，詔節度使孟球募兵三千往屯，以八百人戍桂林。

translations.literal: At first the barbarians raided the Five Circuits, captured Jiaozhi, and an edict ordered Military Governor Meng Qiu to recruit three thousand troops to garrison there, with eight hundred men guarding Guilin.
translations.idiomatic: When barbarians raided the Five Circuits and took Jiaozhi, the court ordered Military Governor Meng Qiu to raise three thousand men for the frontier and post eight hundred at Guilin.

sentences.zh: 舊制，三年一更。

translations.literal: By old regulation they were rotated every three years.
translations.idiomatic: By regulation they were rotated every three years.

sentences.zh: 至期請代，而彥曾親吏尹戡、徐行儉貪不恤士，乃議稟賜乏，請無發兵，復留屯一年。

translations.literal: When the term came they requested relief, but Yanzeng's intimate clerks Yin Kan and Xu Xingjian were greedy and uncaring toward the troops; they therefore argued that stipends and gifts were exhausted, requested that no relief troops be sent, and kept the garrison another year.
translations.idiomatic: When their term ended they asked to be relieved, but Yanzeng's favorites Yin Kan and Xu Xingjian, greedy and indifferent to the men, claimed stipends were exhausted, refused to send replacements, and kept the garrison another year.

sentences.zh: 戍者怒，殺都將王仲甫，脅糧料判官龐勳為將，取庫兵，剽湘、衡，虜丁壯，合眾千餘北還，自浙西趨淮南，達泗口。

translations.literal: The garrison troops grew angry, killed Commandant Wang Zhongfu, and compelled Commissary Judge Pang Xun to be their general; they seized arsenal weapons, plundered Xiang and Heng, seized able-bodied men, gathered more than a thousand and returned north, from Zhexi pressing toward Huainan until they reached Sikou.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison rose in fury, killed Commandant Wang Zhongfu, and forced Commissary Judge Pang Xun to lead them; they seized arsenal arms, raided Xiang and Heng, impressed men, and with more than a thousand followers marched north through Zhexi into Huainan as far as Sikou.

sentences.zh: 所過先遣俳兒弄木偶，伺人情，以防邀遏。

translations.literal: Where they passed they first sent jesters manipulating puppets to probe popular sentiment and guard against interception.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever they marched they sent jesters with puppets ahead to gauge local sentiment and avoid ambush.

sentences.zh: 彥曾命牙將田厚簡慰勞，而用都虞候元密伏甲任山館擊賊。

translations.literal: Yanzeng ordered his yamen general Tian Houjian to offer comfort and rewards, but used Chief Commandant Yuan Mi to set an ambush with armor at Renshan lodge to strike the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzeng sent his yamen general Tian Houjian with gifts of comfort while Chief Commandant Yuan Mi lay in ambush at Renshan lodge to attack the rebels.

sentences.zh: 勳遣吏紿言士思歸，不敢遏，請至府解甲自歸，彥曾斬其吏。

translations.literal: Xun sent an official to deceive them, saying the soldiers wished to return and dared not obstruct them, and asking to come to the prefectural seat to lay down arms and surrender of themselves; Yanzeng beheaded the official.
translations.idiomatic: Xun sent an envoy claiming his men only wanted to go home and asking to surrender at the prefectural seat; Yanzeng had the envoy executed.

sentences.zh: 勳陷宿州，發廥錢募兵，亡命者從亂如歸，船千艘，與騎夾岸，噪而進。

translations.literal: Xun captured Suzhou, issued treasury funds to recruit troops, and outlaws joined the rebellion as if returning home; a thousand boats with cavalry along both banks advanced with a clamor.
translations.idiomatic: Xun took Suzhou, opened the treasury to recruit troops, and outlaws flocked to him; a thousand boats and horsemen along both banks advanced with a roar.

sentences.zh: 彥曾料丁男乘城。

translations.literal: Yanzeng conscripted adult males to man the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzeng drafted every able-bodied man onto the walls.

sentences.zh: 或勸率眾奔兗州，彥曾曰：「我，方帥也，奉命守此，惟有死爾。

translations.literal: Some urged him to lead the crowd and flee to Yanzhou; Yanzeng said: "I am a frontier commander, ordered to guard this place—there is only death.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged him to flee with his followers to Yanzhou; Yanzeng said, "I am a frontier commander ordered to hold this city—death is all that remains.

sentences.zh: 」斬議者一人號於眾。

translations.literal: " He beheaded one who had urged this and displayed the head before the crowd.
translations.idiomatic: " He beheaded one adviser and displayed the head before the troops.

sentences.zh: 俄而勳傅城，城中大霧如墮。

translations.literal: Soon Xun assaulted the walls; within the city a great fog hung as if falling.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xun assaulted the walls while a dense fog seemed to fall over the city.

sentences.zh: 彥曾悉誅賊家屬，勳眾四面超墉入，囚彥曾大彭館。

translations.literal: Yanzeng executed all the bandits' families; Xun's host scaled the walls on four sides and entered, imprisoning Yanzeng in the Great Peng lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzeng had every rebel family executed; Xun's men scaled the walls on all sides, seized the city, and imprisoned Yanzeng in the Great Peng lodge.

sentences.zh: 有曹君長者說勳曰：「貴者不並處，今朝廷未以留後命公，蓋觀察使存爾。

translations.literal: A certain Cao Junzhang advised Xun: "The exalted do not dwell together; now the court has not appointed you acting military commissioner—the observation commissioner is kept alive for that reason.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Cao Junzhang told Xun, "Two men of rank cannot share one seat; the court has not yet made you acting commissioner—that is why the observation commissioner still lives.

sentences.zh: 」勳乃殺彥曾於寢，自監軍使逮官屬皆死。

translations.literal: " Xun then killed Yanzeng in his chamber; from the army supervisory commissioner down, all officials died.
translations.idiomatic: " Xun then killed Yanzeng in his bedchamber, and from the army supervisory commissioner down every official was slain.

sentences.zh: 始，彥曾治第鄭州，引水灌沼，水十步忽化為血。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yanzeng built a mansion in Zhengzhou, he led water to irrigate a pond; within ten paces the water suddenly turned to blood.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while building a mansion in Zhengzhou, he channeled water into a pond that within ten paces suddenly turned to blood.

sentences.zh: 署張佛筵，液蜜為人，一昔鼠齧皆斷首。

translations.literal: He set out a spread for Buddha; figures of men made from liquid honey—in one night rats gnawed and all their heads were severed.
translations.idiomatic: He laid out a Buddhist feast with honey figures of men; overnight rats gnawed off every head.

sentences.zh: 徐有子亭，下瀦水為沱，彥曾導清河灌之，鐫石龍首注溜，蔽以屋。

translations.literal: Xuzhou had the Ziting pavilion; below it impounded water formed a pool; Yanzeng channeled the Clear River to irrigate it, carved a stone dragon head for the outflow, and covered it with a building.
translations.idiomatic: Xuzhou had the Ziting pavilion with a pool below it; Yanzeng diverted the Clear River to fill it, carved a stone dragon head for the outlet, and roofed it over.

sentences.zh: 徐人謂屋覆龍，于文為「龐」；

translations.literal: The people of Xu said a building covering a dragon, written out, forms "Pang";
translations.idiomatic: Locals said a roof over a dragon, written out, spells "Pang";

sentences.zh: 清河，崔望也，為吞噬雲。

translations.literal: the Clear River is the surname Cui looking out, meaning to devour and swallow.
translations.idiomatic: and the Clear River is the Cui clan's domain, signifying devouring and swallowing.

sentences.zh: 贈刑部尚書。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 乾符中，錄其子祐之為滎陽尉。

translations.literal: During Qianfu his son Youzhi was enrolled as magistrate of Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: During Qianfu his son Youzhi was given office as magistrate of Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 徐吏有路審中者，彥曾知其能，頗任之。

translations.literal: Among the Xu officials was Lu Shenzhong; Yanzeng knew his ability and greatly entrusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Among Yanzeng's Xu subordinates was Lu Shenzhong, whom he recognized as capable and relied on heavily.

sentences.zh: 既遇害，賂守卒，斂藏其屍。

translations.literal: After Yanzeng was killed, he bribed the guards, gathered and concealed the corpse.
translations.idiomatic: After Yanzeng was killed, he bribed the guards and secretly recovered and hid the body.

sentences.zh: 張玄稔攻徐州；

translations.literal: Zhang Xuanchen attacked Xuzhou;
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Xuanchen attacked Xuzhou,

sentences.zh: 審中率死士應官軍，開南白門，官兵入，因得破勳。

translations.literal: Shenzhong led dare-to-die troops to join the government army, opened the South White Gate, government troops entered, and thereby Pang Xun was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzhong led dare-to-die troops to the government side, opened the South White Gate, let the imperial army in, and Pang Xun was overthrown.

sentences.zh: 後位嵐州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he held the post of Prefect of Lanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Prefect of Lanzhou.

sentences.zh: 鄭畋謂審中節貫神明，請擢為右羽林將軍，詔可。

translations.literal: Zheng Tian said Shenzhong's integrity penetrated to the spirits; he requested promotion to Right General of the Feathered Forest, and an edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tian said Shenzhong's integrity touched the divine and asked that he be promoted to Right General of the Feathered Forest; the edict approved.

sentences.zh: 有許鐸者，罷武城令，客于徐，勳脅以官，不從。

translations.literal: There was Xu Duo, dismissed as magistrate of Wucheng, lodging in Xu; Xun coerced him with office, but he would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Duo, a dismissed magistrate of Wucheng staying in Xu, refused office when Pang Xun tried to coerce him.

sentences.zh: 彥曾官屬被囚，鐸潛饋資糧，及死，為收瘞，匿免其子弟，賊平，乃皆歸其喪。

translations.literal: Yanzeng's subordinate officials were imprisoned; Duo secretly supplied provisions; when they died he gathered and buried them, concealed and spared their sons and younger brothers, and after the bandits were pacified returned all their coffins.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanzeng's staff were imprisoned, Duo secretly fed them; after they were killed he buried them, hid their sons and brothers, and when the rebellion ended returned every coffin to the families.

sentences.zh: 詔拜石首令，賜銀緋。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him magistrate of Shishou and bestowed silver seals and crimson robes.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made him magistrate of Shishou and bestowed silver seals and crimson robes.

sentences.zh: 僚官焦璐、溫廷皓、李棁、崔蘊、柳秦、盧崇嗣、韋廷範贈官有差，錄其子官之。

translations.literal: Staff officials Jiao Lu, Wen Tinghao, Li Zhuo, Cui Yun, Liu Qin, Lu Chongsi, and Wei Tingfan received posthumous offices in varying grades, and their sons were enrolled in office.
translations.idiomatic: Staff officials Jiao Lu, Wen Tinghao, Li Zhuo, Cui Yun, Liu Qin, Lu Chongsi, and Wei Tingfan received posthumous offices of varying rank, and their sons were given government posts.

sentences.zh: 徐彥伯徐彥伯，兗州瑕丘人，名洪，以字顯。

translations.literal: Xu Yanbo — Xu Yanbo, a native of Xiaqiu in Yanzhou, personal name Hong, known by his style name.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yanbo — Xu Yanbo of Xiaqiu in Yanzhou, personal name Hong, known by his style.

sentences.zh: 七歲能為文。

translations.literal: At seven he could compose texts.
translations.idiomatic: At seven he could already write.

sentences.zh: 結廬太行山下。

translations.literal: He built a hut beneath Mount Taihang.
translations.idiomatic: He built a hut beneath Mount Taihang.

sentences.zh: 薛元超安撫河北，表其賢，對策高第。

translations.literal: When Xue Yuanchao pacified Hebei, he memorialized Yanbo's worth; in the policy-response examination he achieved top standing.
translations.idiomatic: When Xue Yuanchao pacified Hebei he recommended Yanbo's talent; Yanbo took top standing in the policy-response examination.

sentences.zh: 調永壽尉、蒲州司兵參軍。

translations.literal: He was assigned as magistrate of Yongshou and Military Affairs Officer of Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as magistrate of Yongshou and Military Affairs Officer of Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 時司戶韋皓善判，司士李亙工書，而彥伯屬辭，時稱「河東三絕」。

translations.literal: At the time Revenue Registrar Wei Hao was skilled at judgments, Records Officer Li Gen was accomplished at calligraphy, and Yanbo composed literary pieces—they were called the "Three Unmatched of Hedong."
translations.idiomatic: Revenue Registrar Wei Hao excelled at legal judgments, Records Officer Li Gen at calligraphy, and Yanbo at literary composition—they were called the "Three Unmatched of Hedong."

sentences.zh: 遷職方員外郎，奉迎中宗房州，進給事中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Bureau of Personnel Assignments, welcomed Zhongzong from Fangzhou, and advanced to Drafting Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Bureau of Personnel Assignments, escorted Zhongzong back from Fangzhou, and advanced to Drafting Attendant.

sentences.zh: 武后撰《三教珠英》，取文辭士，皆天下選，而彥伯、李嶠居首。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu compiled the "Pearls of the Three Teachings," she selected literary scholars from throughout the realm; Yanbo and Li Jiao stood foremost.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu compiled the "Pearls of the Three Teachings," she chose literary scholars from across the empire; Yanbo and Li Jiao ranked first.

sentences.zh: 遷宗正卿，出為齊州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Imperial Clan Court and sent out as Prefect of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He became Director of the Imperial Clan Court and then Prefect of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 帝復位，改太常少卿。

translations.literal: When the emperor regained the throne, he was made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was restored, he was made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 以脩《武后實錄》勞，封高平縣子。

translations.literal: For his labor in compiling the Veritable Records of Empress Wu, he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Gaoping county.
translations.idiomatic: For helping compile the Veritable Records of Empress Wu, he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 為衛州刺史，政善狀，璽書嘉勞。

translations.literal: As Prefect of Weizhou his governance was excellent; an imperial autograph edict praised and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: As Prefect of Weizhou he governed so well that an autograph edict praised and rewarded him.

sentences.zh: 移蒲州，以近畿，會郊祭，上《南郊賦》一篇，辭致黃縟。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Puzhou; because it was near the capital region, when the suburban sacrifice came he submitted one "Rhapsody on the Southern Suburb," its diction ornate and grand.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Puzhou near the capital, he submitted a "Rhapsody on the Southern Suburb" for the suburban sacrifice, written in ornate, stately prose.

sentences.zh: 擢脩文館學士、工部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Xiūwén Hall academician and Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to Xiūwén Hall academician and Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 曆太子賓客。

translations.literal: He successively served as Guest of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Guest of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 以疾乞骸骨，許之。

translations.literal: On grounds of illness he requested his bones—that is, retirement—and was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire on grounds of illness and was permitted.

sentences.zh: 開元二年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Kaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Kaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 彥伯事寡嫂謹，撫諸侄同己子。

translations.literal: Yanbo served his widowed sister-in-law with care and reared his nephews as his own sons.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo tended his widowed sister-in-law with scrupulous care and raised his nephews as his own sons.

sentences.zh: 秉筆累朝，後來翕然慕仿。

translations.literal: He wielded the brush through successive reigns, and later men all at once admired and imitated him.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote for successive reigns, and later writers imitated him wholesale.

sentences.zh: 晚為文稍強澀，然當時不及也。

translations.literal: In his later years his writing grew somewhat forceful and austere, yet at the time none could match him.
translations.idiomatic: His late style grew somewhat forceful and austere, yet none in his day could match him.

sentences.zh: 始，武后時，大獄興，王公卿士以語言為酷吏所引，死徙不可計。

translations.literal: At the beginning, in Empress Wu's time, great prosecutions arose; princes, dukes, and scholar-officials were implicated by their words through cruel officials, and deaths and banishments were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu great prosecutions arose; princes and officials were ensnared by their own words through cruel officials, and deaths and banishments were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 彥伯著《樞機論》以謂：「言者，德之柄，行之主，志之端，身之文也。

translations.literal: Yanbo wrote the "Treatise on the Pivot of Power," saying: "Speech is the handle of virtue, the master of conduct, the tip of intent, the ornament of the person.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo wrote the "Treatise on the Pivot of Power," arguing, "Speech is the handle of virtue, the master of conduct, the edge of intent, the ornament of the self.

sentences.zh: 君子之樞機，動則物應，得失之見也。

translations.literal: The pivot of power of the gentleman—when it moves, things respond; gain and loss become visible.
translations.idiomatic: A gentleman's pivot of power, once moved, draws response from the world; gain and loss stand revealed.

sentences.zh: 可以濟身，亦以覆身，否泰榮辱一系之。

translations.literal: It can save the person, and also overturn the person; fortune and misfortune, glory and disgrace all hang on it.
translations.idiomatic: It can save a man or destroy him; fortune and ruin, honor and shame all hang upon it.

sentences.zh: 能審思而應，精慮而動，擇其交以後談，則悔吝何由而生？

translations.literal: If one can reflect carefully before responding, deliberate finely before acting, and choose one's associations before speaking afterward—how then could regret and distress arise?
translations.idiomatic: Reflect carefully before you answer, deliberate finely before you act, and choose your company before you speak—how then could regret ever arise?

sentences.zh: 怨惡何由而至？

translations.literal: How then could resentment and hatred come upon one?
translations.idiomatic: How then could resentment and hatred find their way to you?

sentences.zh: 如此乃可以言也。

translations.literal: Only thus may one speak.
translations.idiomatic: Only then is speech safe.

sentences.zh: 」以為戒世雲。

translations.literal: " He offered this as a warning to the age.
translations.idiomatic: " He meant it as a warning to the age.

sentences.zh: 蘇味道蘇味道，趙州欒城人。

translations.literal: Su Weidao — Su Weidao, a native of Luancheng in Zhaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Su Weidao — Su Weidao of Luancheng in Zhaozhou.

sentences.zh: 九歲能屬辭，與裏人李嶠俱以文翰顯，時號「蘇李」。

translations.literal: At nine he could compose literary pieces; with his fellow townsman Li Jiao he both became famous for letters and were called at the time "Su and Li."
translations.idiomatic: At nine he could already write; he and his townsman Li Jiao won fame for their letters and were known as "Su and Li."

sentences.zh: 逮冠，州舉進士，中第。

translations.literal: Upon reaching adulthood he was nominated by the prefecture for the jinshi examination and passed.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age the prefecture nominated him for the jinshi examination and he passed.

sentences.zh: 累調咸陽尉。

translations.literal: He was successively assigned as magistrate of Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted successively as magistrate of Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 吏部侍郎裴行儉才之，會征突厥，引管書記。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Personnel Pei Xingjian recognized his talent; when the campaign against the Turks was launched, he brought Weidao in to manage secretarial records.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Personnel Pei Xingjian recognized his talent and, when the campaign against the Turks began, brought him on as secretary.

sentences.zh: 裴居道為左金吾衛將軍，倩味道作章，攬筆而具，閑徹清密，當時盛傳。

translations.literal: When Pei Judao was General of the Left Golden Crow Guard, he asked Weidao to compose a memorial; taking up the brush he completed it at once, leisurely yet thorough and clear and dense—at the time widely celebrated.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Judao was General of the Left Golden Crow Guard, he asked Weidao to draft a memorial; Weidao took up the brush and finished at once in prose at once leisurely and precise, and the piece was widely admired.

sentences.zh: 延載中，以鳳閣舍人檢校侍郎、同鳳閣鸞台平章事，歲餘為真。

translations.literal: During Yanzai, as Drafting Attendant of the Fengge Office he was made Acting Vice Director and Associate Chief Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery; after more than a year he received the regular appointment.
translations.idiomatic: During Yanzai he served as Fengge Drafting Attendant, Acting Vice Director, and Associate Chief Councilor; after a year he received the regular appointment.

sentences.zh: 證聖元年，與張錫俱坐法系司刑獄。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengsheng, he and Zhang Xi together were implicated by legal cases and imprisoned by the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhengsheng he and Zhang Xi were both implicated in legal cases and imprisoned by the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 錫雖下吏，氣象自如，味道獨席地飯蔬，為危惴可憐者。

translations.literal: Though Xi was placed under arrest, his bearing remained as before; Weidao alone sat on the ground eating vegetables, a figure of fearful dread and pity.
translations.idiomatic: Xi kept his composure even in custody, but Weidao sat on the bare ground eating vegetables, a picture of terrified misery.

sentences.zh: 武后聞，放錫嶺南，才降味道集州刺史。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu heard of this, she released Xi to Lingnan and only demoted Weidao to Prefect of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu heard of it, sent Xi to Lingnan, and demoted Weidao only to Prefect of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 召為天官侍郎。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Vice Director of the Bureau of the Heavenly Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Vice Director of the Bureau of the Heavenly Office.

sentences.zh: 聖曆初，復以鳳閣侍郎、同鳳閣鸞台三品。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenglì he again served as Vice Director of the Fengge Office and Third Rank Associate of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shenglì he again became Fengge Vice Director and Third Rank Associate of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 更葬其親，有詔州縣治喪事。

translations.literal: He reburied his parents; an edict ordered the prefectures and counties to manage the funeral affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When he reburied his parents, an edict ordered local officials to manage the funeral.

sentences.zh: 味道因役庸過程，遂侵毀鄉人墓田，蕭至忠劾之，貶坊州刺史。

translations.literal: Weidao, because corvée laborers passed through on the way, then encroached on and destroyed a fellow townsman's grave fields; Xiao Zhizhong impeached him and he was demoted to Prefect of Fangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée workers passing through his parents' reburial encroached on a neighbor's grave land; Xiao Zhizhong impeached him and he was demoted to Prefect of Fangzhou.

sentences.zh: 遷益州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chief Administrator of the Yizhou Grand Protectorate-General.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Chief Administrator of the Yizhou Grand Protectorate-General.

sentences.zh: 張易之敗，坐黨附，貶眉州刺史。

translations.literal: When Zhang Yizhi fell, Weidao was implicated for party attachment and demoted to Prefect of Meizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yizhi fell, Weidao was punished for associating with his faction and demoted to Prefect of Meizhou.

sentences.zh: 復還益州長史，未就道卒，年五十八，贈冀州刺史。

translations.literal: He was again returned to Chief Administrator of Yizhou but died before taking up the post, aged fifty-eight; posthumously made Prefect of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was restored to Chief Administrator of Yizhou but died before taking up the post, at fifty-eight; he was posthumously appointed Prefect of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 味道練台閣故事，善占奏。

translations.literal: Weidao was versed in Secretariat-Chancellery precedents and skilled at drafting memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Weidao knew Secretariat-Chancellery precedent inside out and excelled at memorials.

sentences.zh: 然其為相，特具位，未嘗有所發明，脂韋自營而已。

translations.literal: Yet as chancellor he merely filled the seat and never advanced any initiative, only greasing and currying favor for himself.
translations.idiomatic: As chancellor he merely filled the seat, advanced no policy, and greased every wheel for his own safety.

sentences.zh: 常謂人曰：「決事不欲明白，誤則有悔，摸棱持兩端可也。

translations.literal: He often told people: "In deciding affairs one should not wish to be clear; if mistaken there is regret—holding the edge and keeping both sides is acceptable."
translations.idiomatic: He often said, "Do not decide matters too clearly; mistakes bring regret—it is safer to stay ambiguous and keep both sides open."

sentences.zh: 」故世號「摸棱手」。

translations.literal: " Therefore the age called him "the edge-feeler."
translations.idiomatic: " Hence his nickname, "the edge-feeler."

sentences.zh: 性友愛。

translations.literal: By nature he was affectionate toward kin.
translations.idiomatic: He was affectionate by nature.

sentences.zh: 其弟味元，味元嘗請托不遂，因慢折之，味道怡然不屑。

translations.literal: His younger brother Weiyuan—Weiyuan once made a request that was not granted and therefore treated him with slow insult; Weidao remained easy and unconcerned.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Weiyuan, when a request went unfulfilled, treated him with contempt; Weidao remained unruffled.

sentences.zh: 所論著行于時。

translations.literal: His writings circulated in his time.
translations.idiomatic: His writings circulated widely in his day.

sentences.zh: 豆盧欽望豆盧欽望，雍州萬年人。

translations.literal: Dou Lu Qinwang — Dou Lu Qinwang, a native of Wannian in Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Lu Qinwang — Dou Lu Qinwang of Wannian in Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖寬，隋文帝外孫，為梁泉令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Kuan was a grandson by marriage of Emperor Wen of Sui and served as magistrate of Liangquan.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Kuan was a grandson-in-law of Emperor Wen of Sui and served as magistrate of Liangquan.

sentences.zh: 高祖定關中，與郡守蕭瑀率豪姓進款。

translations.literal: When Gaozu secured Guanzhong, together with the prefect Xiao Yu he led powerful clans to submit allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu secured Guanzhong, he and Prefect Xiao Yu led the great clans in submission.

sentences.zh: 擢累殿中監。

translations.literal: He was promoted through successive posts to Supervisor of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to Supervisor of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 子懷讓，尚萬春公主。

translations.literal: His son Huairang married Princess Wanchun.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huairang married Princess Wanchun.

sentences.zh: 詔寬用魏太和詔，去「豆」姓，著「盧」。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Kuan to follow the Northern Wei Taihe edict, drop the surname "Dou," and adopt "Lu."
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed the Northern Wei Taihe precedent: Kuan dropped the surname Dou and adopted Lu.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，遷禮部尚書、左衛大將軍，芮國公。

translations.literal: During Zhenguan he was transferred to Minister of Rites and Great General of the Left Guard, Duke of Ruiguo.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhenguan he became Minister of Rites and Great General of the Left Guard with the title Duke of Ruiguo.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈特進、并州都督，陪葬昭陵，諡曰定。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Special Advancement and Protector-General of Bingzhou, buried with attendant honor at Zhaoling, with posthumous title Ding.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Special Advancement and Protector-General of Bingzhou, buried with attendant honor at Zhaoling with the posthumous title Ding.

sentences.zh: 復其舊姓。

translations.literal: His original surname was restored.
translations.idiomatic: His original surname was restored.

sentences.zh: 欽望累官越州都督、司賓卿。

translations.literal: Qinwang successively held the posts of Protector-General of Yuezhou and Director of the Court for Imperial Guests.
translations.idiomatic: Qinwang successively served as Protector-General of Yuezhou and Director of the Court for Imperial Guests.

sentences.zh: 長壽二年，拜內史，封芮國公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Changshou he was appointed Inner Scribe and enfeoffed as Duke of Ruiguo.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Changshou he was appointed Inner Scribe and enfeoffed as Duke of Ruiguo.

sentences.zh: 李昭德被罪，有司劾奏欽望阿順昭德不執正，附臣罔君，貶趙州刺史。

translations.literal: When Li Zhaode was charged with crimes, the relevant offices impeached Qinwang for flattering Zhaode and not upholding rectitude, for a subject attaching to a minister and deceiving the ruler; he was demoted to Prefect of Zhaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zhaode was condemned, officials impeached Qinwang for flattering him rather than upholding justice, for a subject who clung to a minister and misled the throne; he was demoted to Prefect of Zhaozhou.

sentences.zh: 入為司府卿，遷秋官尚書。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury and was transferred to Minister of Autumnal Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury and was promoted to Minister of Autumnal Affairs.

sentences.zh: 中宗還東宮，拜太子宮尹。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong returned to the Eastern Palace, Qinwang was appointed Palace Intendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong returned to the Eastern Palace, Qinwang was appointed Palace Intendant of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 進文昌右相、同鳳閣鸞台三品。

translations.literal: He advanced to Right Chancellor of the Secretariat and Third Rank Associate of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Chancellor of the Secretariat and Third Rank Associate of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 罷為太子賓客。

translations.literal: He was dismissed and made Guest of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed and made Guest of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 帝復位，擢尚書左僕射、平章軍國重事。

translations.literal: When the emperor regained the throne, he was advanced to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs with charge of weighty military and state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was restored, he was made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs with charge of weighty military and state affairs.

sentences.zh: 欽望居宰相積十餘年，方易之、三思等怙勢宣烝，窺間王室，戮忠戚，觖冀非常，不能有所裁抑，獨謹身諄諄自全。

translations.literal: Qinwang held the chancellorship for more than ten years; when Yizhi, Sansi, and others relied on power to spread debauchery, spied for openings against the royal house, slaughtered loyal kin, and coveted extraordinary gains, he could not restrain them in any way and only guarded himself carefully with repeated admonitions to preserve his safety.
translations.idiomatic: Qinwang served as chancellor for more than ten years while Yizhi, Sansi, and their faction abused power, probed the throne's weakness, killed loyal kin, and reached for the extraordinary; he could not check them and only guarded himself with painstaking caution.

sentences.zh: 進開府儀同三司，檢校安國相王府長史。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Grand Master with the Golden Pouch and Acting Chief Administrator of the Anguo Prince of Xiang's establishment.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Master with the Golden Pouch and Acting Chief Administrator of the Anguo Prince of Xiang's establishment.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十，贈司空、并州大都督，陪葬乾陵，諡曰元。

translations.literal: He died, aged eighty, and was posthumously made Minister of Works and Grand Protector-General of Bingzhou, buried with attendant honor at Qianling, with posthumous title Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty and was posthumously appointed Minister of Works and Grand Protector-General of Bingzhou, buried with attendant honor at Qianling with the posthumous title Yuan.

sentences.zh: 武后時，宰相又有史務滋、崔元綜、周允元，略可述者附左方。

translations.literal: In Empress Wu's time there were also the chancellors Shi Wuzi, Cui Yuanzong, and Zhou Yun'yuan; those briefly worth recounting are appended below.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu there were also chancellors Shi Wuzi, Cui Yuanzong, and Zhou Yun'yuan; brief accounts of those worth noting follow.

sentences.zh: 附 史務滋史務滋，宣州溧陽人。

translations.literal: Appendix: Shi Wuzi — Shi Wuzi, a native of Liyang in Xuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Shi Wuzi — Shi Wuzi of Liyang in Xuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 累吏勞，遷司賓卿，進拜納言。

translations.literal: Through accumulated service in clerical labor he was transferred to Director of the Court for Imperial Guests and advanced to Supplicator.
translations.idiomatic: Through long clerical service he became Director of the Court for Imperial Guests and then Supplicator.

sentences.zh: 後革命，詔務滋等十人分行天下。

translations.literal: After the dynastic revolution, an edict ordered Wuzi and nine others to tour the realm in separate circuits.
translations.idiomatic: After the dynastic revolution, an edict sent Wuzi and nine others on separate tours of the realm.

sentences.zh: 雅州刺史劉行實兄弟為侍御史來子珣誣其反，詔務滋與來俊臣雜治，俊臣言務滋與囚善，掩其反狀，後命俊臣並治，遂自殺。

translations.literal: The brothers Liu Xingshi and Liu Xingmin, prefect of Yazhou, were slandered for rebellion by Attending Censor Lai Zixun; an edict ordered Wuzi and Lai Jun'chen to try the case jointly. Jun'chen said Wuzi was friendly with the prisoners and concealed their rebellious conduct; later he was ordered to try the case together with Jun'chen alone, and Wuzi then killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Liu Xingshi and his brother were accused of rebellion by Attending Censor Lai Zixun; Wuzi and Lai Jun'chen were ordered to try the case together. Jun'chen claimed Wuzi favored the prisoners and hid evidence of rebellion; when the court left Jun'chen in sole charge, Wuzi killed himself.

sentences.zh: 附 崔元綜崔元綜，鄭州新鄭人。

translations.literal: Appendix: Cui Yuanzong — Cui Yuanzong, a native of Xinzheng in Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Cui Yuanzong — Cui Yuanzong of Xinzheng in Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖君肅，武德中為黃門侍郎、鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: His grandfather Junsu, during Wude, served as Vice Director of the Yellow Gate and Director of the Court for Dependencies.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Junsu served under Wude as Vice Director of the Yellow Gate and Director of the Court for Dependencies.

sentences.zh: 元綜，天授初以鸞台侍郎、同鳳閣鸞台平章事。

translations.literal: Yuanzong, at the beginning of Tianshou, served as Vice Director of the Luan Terrace and Associate Chief Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianshou Yuanzong served as Luan Terrace Vice Director and Associate Chief Councilor.

sentences.zh: 性恪慎，坐政事堂，束帶，終日不休偃，尤護細概。

translations.literal: By nature he was scrupulous and cautious; sitting in the Hall of Government Affairs he kept his belt fastened and never rested the whole day, especially guarding minute details.
translations.idiomatic: Scrupulous by nature, he sat in the Hall of Government Affairs with belt fastened and never rested all day, guarding every minute detail.

sentences.zh: 外若謹厚，而中刻薄。

translations.literal: Outwardly he seemed careful and generous, but inwardly he was harsh and mean.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly he seemed careful and generous, but inwardly he was harsh and mean.

sentences.zh: 每受制鞫獄，必澡垢索疵，不入死不肯止，人畏鄙之。

translations.literal: Whenever he received orders to interrogate cases, he always scrubbed for dirt and sought flaws; unless the accused entered death he would not stop—people feared and despised him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever ordered to interrogate a case, he hunted for every flaw and would not stop short of a death sentence; men feared and despised him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，坐事流振州，搢紳為慶。

translations.literal: Before long, on a charge he was banished to Zhenzhou, and the gentry rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was banished to Zhenzhou on a charge, to the relief of the gentry.

sentences.zh: 會赦還，除監察御史。

translations.literal: When an amnesty came he returned and was made Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty brought him back, and he was made Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 遷蒲州刺史，致仕。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Prefect of Puzhou and retired.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Prefect of Puzhou and retired from office.

sentences.zh: 善攝生，年九十餘卒。

translations.literal: He was skilled at nurturing life and died in his nineties.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled at nurturing his health, he died in his nineties.

sentences.zh: 附 周允元周允元字汝良，豫州安城人。

translations.literal: Appendix: Zhou Yun'yuan — Zhou Yun'yuan, style name Ruliang, a native of Ancheng in Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Zhou Yun'yuan — Zhou Yun'yuan, styled Ruliang, of Ancheng in Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 自右肅政御史中丞，拜檢校鳳閣侍郎、同鳳閣鸞台平章事。

translations.literal: From Censor-in-Chief of the Right Office for Scrutinizing Governance, he was appointed Acting Vice Director of the Fengge Office and Associate Chief Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: From Censor-in-Chief of the Right Office for Scrutinizing Governance he was appointed Acting Fengge Vice Director and Associate Chief Councilor.

sentences.zh: 武后宴宰相，詔陳書傳善言，允元曰：「恥其君不如堯、舜。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu feasted the chancellors, she ordered them to set forth fine sayings from the classics; Yun'yuan said: "One is ashamed if one's ruler is not like Yao and Shun."
translations.idiomatic: At a feast for her chancellors, Empress Wu asked each to cite a fine saying from the classics; Yun'yuan said, "It is shameful when one's ruler falls short of Yao and Shun."

sentences.zh: 」武三思劾奏語指斥，後曰：「聞其言足以誡，安得為過？

translations.literal: " Wu Sansi memorialized that the words were accusatory and pointed; the empress said: "Hearing his words is enough for admonition—how can this be fault?"
translations.idiomatic: " Wu Sansi accused the remark of being a pointed rebuke; the empress said, "His words are admonition enough—how can that be fault?"

sentences.zh: 」卒，贈貝州刺史。

translations.literal: " He died and was posthumously made Prefect of Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: " He died and was posthumously appointed Prefect of Beizhou.
